chunks: ʿAlī ibn Muḥammad, from some of our companions, from ʿUbays ibn Hishām, said: ʿUmar al-Rummānī narrated to me, from Fayḍ ibn al-Mukhtār, who said:

I was in the presence of Abū ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام when Abū al-Ḥasan Mūsā عليه السلام came forward, and he was a boy. So I embraced him and kissed him, and Abū ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام said: “You are the ship, and this one is its captain.”

He said: So I performed hajj the following year, and I had with me two thousand dinars. So I sent one thousand to Abū ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام and one thousand to him. Then when I entered upon Abū ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام, he said: “O Fayḍ, you made him equal to me.” I said: “I only did that because of your statement.” So he said: “Indeed, by Allah, it was not I who did that; rather Allah, Mighty and Majestic, did that for him.”

key_terms.أَبُو الْحَسَنِ مُوسَى: Abū al-Ḥasan Mūsā, Imam Mūsā al-Kāẓim عليه السلام
key_terms.أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ: Abū ʿAbd Allāh, the Imam Jaʿfar al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام in this report
key_terms.أَلْفَا دِينَارٍ: two thousand dinars, indicating a substantial sum of money
key_terms.السَّفِينَةُ: the ship; a metaphor for the community or cause being guided
key_terms.اللَّهُ عَزَّ وَجَلَّ: Allah, Mighty and Majestic, the one who granted this station
key_terms.عَدَلْتَهُ بِي: you equated him with me, meaning you treated him as equal in status
key_terms.مَلَّاحُهَا: its captain or navigator, indicating leadership and direction

ai.seo_question: How does this hadith indicate the Imamate of Abū al-Ḥasan Mūsā عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith narrates an indication by Abū ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام toward the status of Abū al-Ḥasan Mūsā عليه السلام while he was still a boy. It presents a symbolic expression of leadership and shows that the rank granted to him was by Allah, Mighty and Majestic, not by human appointment alone.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Muhammad, from one of our companions, from Ubeys Bin Hisham who said, ‘Umro Al Rummany narrated to me, from Fayz Bin Al Mukhtar who said,

‘I was in the presence of Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> when Abu Al-Hassan Musa<sup>asws</sup> came over, and he<sup>asws</sup> was a boy. So he<sup>asws</sup> embraced him<sup>asws</sup> and kissed him<sup>asws</sup>, and Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘You are the ship and this one<sup>asws</sup> is its captain’.

He (the narrator) said, ‘So I performed Hajj the next year and with me were two thousand Dinars. So I sent a thousand over to Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> and a thousand to him<sup>asws</sup> (Musa<sup>asws</sup>). So when I went over to Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘O Fayz! You equated him<sup>asws</sup> with me<sup>asws</sup>’. I said, ‘But rather, I did that due to your<sup>asws</sup> words’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘But, by Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, it was not I<sup>asws</sup> who did that, but (it was) Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic who Did it with him<sup>asws</sup>’.
en.sarwar: 16. Ali ibn Muhammad has narrated from one of our people from ‘Ubays ibn Hisham that ‘Umar al-Rummaniy narrated to from Fayd ibn al-Mukhtar the following.

“Once when I was in the presence of abu ‘Abdallah (a.s.) that abu al-Hassan Musa (a.s.) came and he was a young boy. I held and kissed him. Abu ‘Abdallah (a.s.) said, “You are the ark and he is the captain.”

The narrator has said that he wen to perform Hajj next year and I had two thousand Dinars. I sent one thousand toabu ‘Abdallah (a.s.) and one thousand to him (abu al-Hassan). When went to see abu ‘Abdallah (a.s.) he said, “You have considered him equal to me.” I said, “I did so because of your words.” He then said, “I swear by Allah, I did not do so, in fact, Allah, the Most Holy, the Most High, has done it for him (abu al-Hassan Musa (a.s.).”
